key_gap: Both rejected the AuraSync pilot as pitched, demanded a reformulated risky claim, and killed the 7.83 Hz physics (~8 orders of magnitude below thermal noise) — the AI reached the identical verdict by running its full pipeline. The human won on the style's home ground by making the falsifiability test the opening, single instrument: it demanded the vendor 'name the observation that would prove the band false,' demonstrated the claim is a prediction-proof net (every outcome — better, unchanged, worse — is explained), and wielded the asymmetry of verification ('one clean falsification outweighs ten thousand confirmations') to discard all 4,000 testimonials and the vendor's circular self-made instrument. The AI buried the falsifier audit inside WHY as one of several checks, so its decisiveness arrived late and the risk-free-confirmation argument was never stated as a principle.
learning_signal: The falsifiability test is not one check among many — on claims that 'look scientific,' it is the decisive instrument and should be the opening move: for the leading claim, state the observation that would refute it; if every possible outcome is compatible, the claim is a prediction-proof net and must be reformulated into a risky form before any testing or funding. Confirmation-type evidence (testimonials, self-made uncalibrated instruments) carries zero weight because it took no risk — the asymmetry of verification. A practical exploit: the claimant's willingness to accept a pre-registered design with an acceptable negative outcome is itself evidence; refusal to be put at risk is an answer.
suggested_improvement: Add a first-class 'falsifier gate' to the WHY stage, run before hypotheses are weighted: for the claim under evaluation write (a) the single observation that would refute it, (b) the list of possible outcomes all of which it can absorb (prediction-proof net check — if the list is non-empty and comprehensive, declare the claim unfalsifiable as stated), (c) the risky reformulation that makes it testable, and (d) an evidence-weight audit that scores each evidence item by the risk it took. Promote the gate into WHAT for any claim that 'looks scientific' (mechanism jargon, testimonials, instruments); record the gate output verbatim in the decision packet.

key_gap: The pure style was nihilistic exactly as its registry entry predicts: it demanded a single decisive falsifier for 'CO2 is the dominant cause of warming,' found that no one observation can be decisive in a noisy system, discounted all the accumulated likelihood-ratio evidence (fingerprint sign pattern, <1% vs ~100% attribution likelihoods) as 'mere corroboration,' refused to attach a probability, and left the policymaker with no position. The AI treated the unit of falsification as the pattern over time, not the single observation: it computed the likelihood ratio (>100:1), recognized that the troposphere-warming/stratosphere-cooling fingerprint is a discriminating observation that would have refuted the claim if absent, and preserved falsifiability by pre-committing to downgrade conditions (stratospheric warming, a decade plateau under rising CO2, fingerprint failure in re-analysis) — delivering 'yes, dominant, ~95%, with exit conditions' instead of a refusal.
learning_signal: For probabilistic claims, the demand for a single decisive falsifier is the error — it is nihilism, not rigor. Falsifiability must be preserved at the pattern level: (1) identify the discriminating observation the evidence would have had to show to refute the claim (e.g., the opposite fingerprint sign pattern); (2) convert evidence into likelihood ratios rather than confirm/falsify verdicts; (3) pre-commit to 2-3 observable downgrade conditions with the confidence drop they would trigger — a claim with declared exit conditions is falsifiable in spirit even when no individual observation can settle it; a claim whose believers cannot name what would weaken it is the unfalsifiable one.
suggested_improvement: In HOW verification for inherently noisy/probabilistic domains, replace the binary falsifier check with a 'commitment contract': (a) compute the likelihood ratio of the top hypothesis vs its best alternative, (b) state the observation or pattern that would most discriminate them (including the sign-pattern that would refute), and (c) pre-register 2-3 downgrade triggers with the confidence-point drop each would cause. Emit the contract as a decision-packet field ('falsification_conditions') so every confident conclusion ships with its exit conditions; treat inability to state downgrade triggers as a red flag equivalent to unfalsifiability.
